cells.tense: At the moment the shape of a job comes clear, the moving is already underway.
cells.ask: Put the pattern you keep noticing on one page, with one thing you'll do from it this week.
cells.core:
Not much is forcing your hand just now. What you want and what you're doing are pointed the same way, so the work moves without you having to shove it. The shape of a situation comes clear and you act on the shape, not on every detail inside it.

Here is what can tip: a rhythm that has settled can also sit. You're free to feed this next, and it stays optional. So put the pattern down where someone else can see it — not the details, the shape — and name one thing you'll do because of it, this week.

When your read of a situation holds up in someone else's hands, the satisfaction you get is real and not borrowed. The rest stays yours to use however the shape shifts.

cells.tense: Ahead of the work sits a version where everyone already understands it, and you are standing there.
cells.ask: Before the next time you lay it out, write what the pattern shows and one thing it doesn't yet.
cells.core:
You're explaining the shape of something before it's had the work of showing itself. The whole picture gets built ahead of the parts that would prove it, and then the picture is defended. Steady forward motion turns into pushing.

What gets spent is the thing the rhythm would have handed you for free — the doing feeling like its own reward. What's left is a future only you can see yet, and each time you lay it out you're trying to get someone into it.

The way back is sorting, not forcing: what you know, kept apart from what you've decided. Before the next time you lay it out, put down what the pattern shows and one thing it doesn't yet. Whatever you can't check stays off the page until it can be. That sorting steadies you even if the picture turns out different than you thought.

cells.tense: Back at an earlier point the shape stopped feeling trustworthy, and you are still parked near there.
cells.ask: Take one finished effort and name what it left behind that still holds today.
cells.core:
Reading how things fit together was not the problem — that comes through fine. Acting on it is what stalled. Now you wait for the picture to be certain, and certainty doesn't arrive, so nothing the pattern tells you gets used.

Don't push energy back into the pattern-reading itself; that side is empty. Go to what sits next to it instead. There were attempts of yours that ended, and the endings were real. What went unaccounted for is what they grew.

Take one of them — not the whole history, one thing — and name what it left you that still holds today. Not what would have been better done. What in fact is still there. That account is how moving from what you feel gets its footing back.

cells.tense: The pattern-reading is running right now, and you're calling it the situation showing what it is.
cells.ask: Where you'd say the project needed this, say "I read it that way" instead.
cells.core:
You already do the thing this is about. A situation starts to move, you take its shape, and your direction comes out of that — it's how your choices get made. What's missing is that you say so out loud. The call keeps getting credited to the project, to the timing, to what obviously had to happen.

Missing ownership here doesn't look like confusion. It looks like accuracy, which is why it lasts.

So the next time you catch yourself saying what this thing needs — the plan, the moment, the work — say instead that you read it that way. Once. You can be wrong; that isn't the claim. It's putting your own name on your read before someone else names it for you. Then it's yours to build on and to revise when the shape changes.
